rows.question: Why does a surfer in a black wetsuit squat on a white surfboard?
rows.prediction:
A surfer in a black wetsuit squatting on a white surfboard is likely in the process of paddling out to catch a wave. Paddling out is an essential part of surfing, as it allows the surfer to reach the lineup where they can catch waves.

When paddling out, surfers typically lie flat on their surfboards with their chest on the board and their legs trailing behind. This position allows them to use their arms to propel themselves through the water more efficiently. Squatting on the surfboard is a common position for surfers when they are paddling out, as it provides better balance and control over the board.

Once the surfer reaches the lineup, they will likely stand up on the surfboard and begin to catch waves. The squatting position is just one part of the process of getting ready to surf, and it is a necessary step in order to reach the lineup and start catching waves.
